conviction_note: Q4 itself is almost entirely pre-guided: FY26 reported sales $675-690M less 9M $511.2M, and management said Q3+Q4 would land at the mid-to-high end. So the print turns on the FY27 guide. Since the July call oil has gone from about $70 back to about $100, EUR/USD has fallen from the 1.17 assumption to 1.12, and the CEO said in July it would be 'unwise' to guide the next year. All of that leans negative. But the stock has already fallen from $265 to $197 almost tick-for-tick inverse with oil, so I put p_up at 45 rather than lower. abs_move is 7.0: the history median is 5.85 with a max of 10.65, a first FY guide pushes it up, and a 9.6% option-implied move from a 33%-spread, 599-OI chain is too thin to anchor on. Findings sum -1.6 against a scaled -0.7. They agree in sign; the gap is the drawdown already in the price.
bar: Reported quarter: company FY26 guidance (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-07-09, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513226000059/wdfc-20260709xexx991.htm). Reported net sales $675-690M and non-GAAP EPS $6.05-6.35, against 9M net sales of $511.2M, imply Q4 net sales of $163.8-178.8M vs $163.5M a year earlier (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513225000061/wdfc-20251022xexx991.htm). 9M GAAP net income was $68.0M (about $5.04 a share at 13.5M shares, about $5.11 adjusted for the $1.3M catch-up amortization, my arithmetic), which implies Q4 non-GAAP EPS of roughly $0.94-1.24 vs $1.56 GAAP a year earlier. Street, ONE source and stale: stockanalysis.com, data last updated 2026-07-16 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wdfc/forecast/): FY26 revenue $683.0M (implied Q4 about $171.8M) and EPS $6.22; FY27 revenue $727.1M and EPS $6.47; 4-5 analysts. The FY27 bar is single-source and set before oil re-spiked, so guidance findings are capped small.

From weekly closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WDFC?range=6mo&interval=1wk) the stock went from $264.91 in the week of 2026-07-06 to $189.29 in the week of 2026-09-14, the inverse of crude ($69-71 to $100).

findings.finding: Management said on the Q3 call (2026-07-09) that Q3 and Q4 'combined' would land in the 'mid- to higher end of our guidance range' and that Q4 would be 'the second strongest quarter of the year'. The mid-to-high end of the $675-690M reported FY range implies Q4 net sales of about $172-179M (+5-9% vs $163.5M). The single stale Street figure ($683M FY, so about $171.8M Q4) sits at the low end of that. The offset: roughly $3M of Q4 demand was pulled into Q3, and that is already in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints (-4.04, -6.63, -0.70, -8.17, -5.85). The only large rise, +10.65 on 2026-07-09, came on a 24% sales beat with a raised bottom end of the guide. An in-line quarter has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and inside the guided range, so it is mostly priced. If the market had fully priced 'mid-to-high end', the only consensus figure found would sit at about $175M+ for Q4 rather than at the $683M FY low-mid point. The gap is small.
findings.independence: Same call as the next two findings. The FY guide numbers come from the 8-K exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513226000059/wdfc-20260709xexx991.htm, which is the same company source.

findings.finding: On 2026-07-09 the CFO said input costs (specialty chemicals and base oils, up 50-100% at the peak) had begun pulling back 20-25% in June and would pace back to pre-war levels 'assuming things don't escalate further in the Middle East'. The CEO said there may be 'a couple of quarters' before gross margin is re-established and that further pricing may be needed in FY27. Since then crude has gone from $68.78-71.41 (weeks of Jun 29 / Jul 6) back to $101.79 (week of Oct 19). That undercuts the FY27 gross-margin recovery that the July-vintage FY27 consensus (EPS $6.47, +4%) assumed, against the company's new target of gross margin 'above 55%'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: October 2025: an FY26 guide calling for gross margin of 55.5-56.5% and growth of 5-12% bought +2.77. January 2026 (-6.63) and April 2026 (-4.04) were sold. July 2026: raising the bottom end of the guide while warning of near-term margin pressure bought +10.65. The guide line moves this stock in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and sized for that. Since mid-July the stock has fallen about 25% in close inverse step with crude, so the market has visibly priced some of the oil damage. The stockanalysis.com consensus snapshot, last updated 2026-07-16, still shows FY27 EPS of $6.47 set at $70 oil. The decline since July could mean the market expects a guide below that, so whether the guide surprises depends on how far the Street has cut, which I could not source.
findings.independence: Crude weekly closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CL=F?range=6mo&interval=1wk (market data, independent of the company). The 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-05-31 says the oil-driven cost impacts 'are expected to be most significant during the fourth quarter': https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513226000061/wdfc-20260531.htm. The transmission from crude to WD-40's inputs is confirmed by the company, but the scale of the re-spike's effect is my inference, so this is a proxy.

findings.finding: Asked on the Q3 call about FY27 margins, CEO Steve Brass said 'I think it would be unwise for us to guide the next fiscal year given the volatility of the situation at the moment'. The company normally issues full-year guidance with its Q4 release: on 2025-10-22 it guided FY26 sales growth of 5-9%, gross margin of 55.5-56.5% and EPS of $5.75-6.15. A withheld, unusually wide or conservative FY27 guide is a live risk. The CFO also hands over to a new CFO on 2026-11-02, so the outgoing CFO sets the first guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every October print in the baseline came with an FY guide (2025-10-22, +2.77). There is no precedent in the baseline for a print without a guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Wire previews carry the FY26 numbers and the Q4 pull-forward, not this remark from the Q&A. If the market expected no guide, a 'perpetual compounder' would trade with a larger risk premium and the Street would show an FY27 range rather than a point estimate. The one source found shows $6.47 as a point estimate.
findings.independence: The CFO transition is in a separate document: 8-K EX-99.1 filed 2026-09-03, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513226000068/exh9911.htm (Keith Stauffer becomes CFO on 2026-11-02; Hyzer stays CFO through the FY26 10-K). The volatility behind the remark is the same oil fact as the previous finding, so the two are related and sized small to avoid double-counting.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide assumed EUR/USD of about 1.17 in Q4. The pair closed at 1.1422 (June), 1.1524 (July) and 1.1589 (August), and stands at 1.1226 on 2026-10-21. EIMEA is 34% of sales, so there is a small headwind to Q4 reported sales against the guide and a larger one to a reported-currency FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated in the baseline. In Q3, FX added about $7.3M (+4 points) to reported sales.
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public, but sell-side FY27 revenue of $727M (stockanalysis.com, 2026-07-16) was set when EUR/USD was near 1.17. It is a small translation effect, sized small.
findings.independence: The guide's 1.17 assumption is in the 8-K EX-99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/105132/000010513226000059/wdfc-20260709xexx991.htm.

findings.finding: The 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-05-31 says the oil-driven COGS impacts are 'expected to be most significant during the fourth quarter'. The CFO said Q3's 56.6% gross margin was held up by inventory bought before the cost rise. FY gross margin guidance of 54.5-55.5% implies a Q4 gross margin well below Q3's (roughly low 50s, my inference), with European and APAC price increases of mid-to-high single digits only reaching the back half of Q4. This is guided, so the reported Q4 margin is expected to be weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026 (-6.63) and April 2026 (-4.04) prints were sold. Q3's beat on margin was bought.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside the guide, so it sits near zero. The residual is whether Q4 margin lands at the low end, because inventory bought in March-May at peak cost flows through, or better, because crude fell to about $69 in late June and discretionary cuts protected EPS. That is not knowable from public data.
findings.independence: The transcript (same company) has the CFO's remark that costs would 'begin to flow through in the fourth quarter' and that discretionary spending was cut in Q4 to protect the bottom line: https://s25.q4cdn.com/753208278/files/doc_financials/2026/q3/312452_2006106219_3761274_Transcript_EditedCopy_20260709233710.pdf

findings.finding: On 2026-06-15 the board authorised a new $100.0M buyback, effective 2026-09-01 with no expiry. That is about 3.8% of a roughly $2.66B market cap (13.5M shares at $197), and the stock has since traded about 25% below its July level, so the call may disclose early-Q1 FY27 repurchases or an accelerated pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. Q3 repurchases were small ($6.8M, 31,250 shares).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public. The pace, which the market cannot see until the call, is what is not priced. It is small against the guide.

outside_window.finding: CFO transition: Keith Stauffer (formerly Galderma US CFO) becomes CFO on 2026-11-02 and Sara Hyzer moves to President, Americas. It could reset FY27 guidance style later in the year.

baseline_tension: The skew is balanced at +0.3 and gives no direction. My negative lean on the FY27 guide agrees with the 25% drawdown since July, which is why it is sized small: the oil-driven damage I identify is visibly in the price already, and the open question is only whether the guide undershoots a Street that has probably cut since its July estimates.
